# nonValidLocale

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** a locale code.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonValidLocale() — Checks whether a value is **not** a locale code. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/string</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonValidLocale(value: string): boolean;
```

`nonValidLocale(value)` is the same test as `!isValidLocale(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

Exactly two ASCII letters, in either case — `"en"`, `"UK"`. A region or a script subtag, as in `"en-US"`, is rejected: this is the short language code, not a full BCP 47 tag.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type     | Description         |
| :-------- | :------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `string` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not a locale code; otherwise `false`.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonValidLocale("en-US"); // => true
nonValidLocale("eng"); // => true
nonValidLocale(""); // => true
nonValidLocale("en"); // => false
nonValidLocale("UK"); // => false
```
